guides.favoredWhen: Teemo wins by farming to boots and punishing Q cooldowns with brief autos; Aatrox wins any post-6 all-in and every full sweet-spot combo.

keyTips.text: Farm safely until Teemo has boots. His Q is nearly impossible to dodge on foot, so concede pressure early rather than bleeding health before Teemo can move.
keyTips.heading: Boots first

keyTips.text: After dodging his Q, land a few autos or a Q and then back off. The cooldown window is short, and staying longer turns a won exchange into his full combo.
keyTips.heading: Window trading

keyTips.text: Track his W at all times. It is his main way to force the combo when Teemo holds an escape, so keep the wave near the middle and always leave room to run from the pull.
keyTips.heading: Respect the pull

tips.text: Prioritize dodging Q sweet spots over dealing damage. Leave the center of W the moment it lands, since the knock-up into Q chain is the entire lane threat.
tips.heading: Dodge first

tips.text: Never start a short trade close to his turret while abilities are down. He chases Teemo down in that space with cooldowns to spare, so only trade with an exit already planned.
tips.heading: No turret trades

tips.text: Do not all-in him after level 6 unless Ignite is ready. Without it the extended fight favors him through R healing, so treat Ignite as the permission slip for every mid-game commit.
tips.heading: Ignite rule

tips.text: Farm and scale instead of forcing kills. Teemo cannot match his R combo in a fair duel, so hold CS parity and let boots plus levels do the work.
tips.heading: Scale it out

tips.text: Win by denying the full combo, not by out-dueling him. Every fight Teemo takes should be a dodged Q into autos and out; the moment he lands a clean three-cast rotation, the lane is lost.
tips.heading: Deny the rotation

tips.text: Keep the wave short after level 6. His kill pattern needs room to chase through W into Q, and a short lane plus shroomed exits starves exactly that.
tips.heading: Short lane

itemization.text: Rush boots before anything else, with Swifties first. Movement speed is the whole dodge plan against Q, so complete them before trading with intent.
Take Ignite over anything defensive. The post-6 all-in only exists with it, and without it Teemo has no way to answer his R healing in the one fight that matters.

keyTips.text: Play the weaker early game for farm and wave control toward Liandry's: take one safe auto when an opponent steps up for a minion, then disengage instead of following into their engage range.
Save Q for opponents who rely on basic attacks or the moment they commit, since the blind stops basic attacks rather than most abilities.

Spend one shroom per wave only when it buys a useful recall or rotation; keep charges for escape routes and objectives, and start objective traps about a minute before Dragon or Baron when the team can safely enter.

tips.text: Collect Dark Harvest stacks only when they cost no death and no missed wave; steady poke matters less than staying alive and on schedule.
Keep the wave near your side when walking up is dangerous, and when safe push fully before recalling, warding ahead of a hard push.
Start Doran's Ring, two Health Potions, and a Stealth Ward; max E first, Q second, and W last, taking R at levels six, eleven, and sixteen, with E-Q-E-W as the example opening.
Maintain distance with W and pre-placed escape-route shrooms before trouble starts rather than reacting after the enemy commits.
Push a safe wave before rotating, but never push deep near an objective spawn or while several opponents are missing.
Trap river entrances, corners, walls, and likely jungle paths, spreading charges across approaches so one Sweeper clears less, and hold one or two charges for the fight itself.
Ward objectives with Control Wards and consider Oracle Lens after lane; shrooms aid vision but never replace real wards.
When behind, farm safely and trap your own jungle entrances; never enter fog alone, and let opponents walk through the traps before helping contest after they back off.
Scale through safe farm into AP and shroom damage, weakening opponents on their approaches before Dragon or Baron fights rather than forcing plays early.
Value staying alive and on schedule over extra Dark Harvest stacks or kills; the shroom field becomes the main threat as items arrive.

itemization.text: Run Dark Harvest with Cheap Shot, Grisly Mementos, and Ultimate Hunter plus Absolute Focus and Gathering Storm; take safe stacks since shroom slows trigger Cheap Shot, Grisly Mementos feeds trinket uptime, and Ultimate Hunter means more frequent shrooms.

Build Liandry's Torment for max-health burn, Malignance for mana plus more frequent shrooms with magic-resistance reduction in its ground, then Shadowflame for the damage increase against targets below forty percent health, buying Sorcerer's Shoes when recall gold allows.

Into substantial purchased magic resistance follow the core with Void Staff and Rabadon's Deathcap, or Deathcap first without much resistance; take Gluttonous Greaves over Sorcerer's only for sustain games with no enemy Ignite and little other healing reduction.
